title: edgecase-hitcurve-optimizer-microburst-scenarios-jul-2024
summary: Exploratory spreadsheet modeling how microburst traffic and heavy tail prefix distributions affect effective KV/prefix cache hit curves. Tests several mitigations (adaptive TTL, probabilistic admission, burst-aware prefetch) and estimates monthly token cost delta vs baseline hosted config.
assumptions: Baseline hosted token cost = $0.000020 per generated token (unit for model compute)
Median request token output = 30 tokens; request size variance captured in scenario multipliers
Traffic has 'microburst' events: 10% of minutes have 5x baseline qps for 1-3 minutes
Prefix reuse skew: 60% of requests share top-1k prefixes, long tail beyond top-10k with low reuse
KV cache capacity limited to 128K entries in typical Dedicated pod; eviction LRU
No additional model quantization savings modeled here (isolating cache effects)

key_takeaways: 1) Microbursts materially reduce observed hit rate vs steady-state—optimizations that adapt to rapid QPS changes (adaptive TTL + burst prefetch) recover the most effective hits. 2) Probabilistic admission improves steady-state but is less effective during short, intense bursts. 3) For our assumed unit token price, moving from baseline to burst-prefetch+adaptive yields ~35% monthly cost improvement on model compute for the modeled workload. 4) Long-tail-heavy customer cohorts will not benefit from prefix caching alone; consider prefix clustering + reranking or model-level caching.
next_steps: Instrument microburst detector in serving runtime to capture minute-level qps spikes (SLO: detect 90% of bursts >3x baseline)
A/B test adaptive-TTL + prefetch in a dedicated pool with synthetic microburst traffic (2-week run)
Add a 'long-tail cohort' flag to Optimize UI so customers can see likely ROI before enabling prefix cache
Run more granular sim across token-size distributions (10/30/100 tokens) and a second model of unit token cost
